thesis_summary.thesis: WhiteHawk Minerals Corp. (NYSE: WHK) is a natural gas mineral and royalty company. **[Fact]** It owns non-operated mineral and royalty interests concentrated in the Marcellus Shale (Appalachian Basin) and the Haynesville Shale (Haynesville Basin), two of the lowest-cost U.S. natural gas basins, and it collects a royalty share of wellhead revenue without operating any wells itself. **[Fact, 424B4 prospectus and investor-relations site]** The company grew mainly by acquisition, closing the PHX Minerals acquisition on June 23, 2025 and the Three Rivers Royalty ("TRR") acquisition, which is why pro forma full-year 2025 revenue ($89.2 million) is roughly nine times larger than actual 2024 revenue ($9.5 million). **[Fact]** WhiteHawk completed its initial public offering on June 10, 2026, raising about $200.2 million in gross proceeds from the sale of 7,700,000 Class A shares at $26.00 per share, through an operating partnership ("Up-C") structure, and simultaneously internalized its management function by buying out its external manager for $130.0 million. **[Fact]**
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: WhiteHawk is a newly public, thinly followed natural gas mineral and royalty aggregator with no analyst estimates or dividend history yet, so any mispricing today is more likely to come from a lack of coverage than from a mispriced narrative. **[Opinion]** The 424B4 prospectus discloses a company-defined non-GAAP measure, Cash Available for Distribution, that reached $36.3 million on a pro forma full-year 2025 basis; against a roughly $600 million pro forma equity value at the $26.00 IPO price, that implies a mid-single-digit percent cash yield before any dividend has actually been declared. **[Fact]** Whether the market is right to wait for the first declared dividend, or is over-discounting a business that already has audited, filed cash flow, is the open question; we do not yet have enough evidence to call it either way. **[Opinion]** The company also restated its FY2025 financial statements on April 22, 2026, seven weeks before the IPO, for material accounting errors, and identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting; that is a real reason a cautious market could discount the stock beyond what the underlying royalty cash flow alone would suggest. **[Fact, 424B4 Risk Factors]**
